newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 5.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Former world champion Australian swimmer Hayley Lewis looks to abandon her swimming career to pursue triathlons. Lewis ceased training in January to rejuvenate herself and do some triathlon races, but has since turned this off season training into a serious pursuit. Page 18.

Australian Rules footballer Tony McGuinness and the Sydney Swans yesterday resolved their dispute over the Club's failure to nominate the former Adelaide captain in their draft two weeks ago. It is believed the Swans and McGuiness's manager, Greg Griffin, negotiated a settlement for as much as $100,000 in Adelaide at the weekend. Page 18.

Melbourne Knights soccer sweeper, Joe Simunic is considering an offer which would make him the highest paid player in the 20-year history of the national soccer league. Simunic, 18, confirmed yesterday new Ericsson Cup club-in-waiting Carlton have approaced him with a deal believed to be around A$100,000. Page 17.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia's spin duo of Shane Warne and Michael Bevan caused a massive upset in South Africa's batting on the final morning at the first cricket Test in Johannesburg, delivering the Australian cricket side to victory by an innings and 196 runs. Warne's 4-3 and Bevan's 4-32 saw the final four wickets fall in just two overs. The final five wickets fell for three runs as South Africa collapsed from 5-127 to 130 all out. Page 48.

Australia's Test cricket matches and one-day series against England later this year are unprecedentedly popular, with the first four days of the second Test - June 19 to 22 - already sold out, as is the third and final one-day match on Sunday, May 25. Pag 48.

An ongoing feud between some of Macedonia's top players and national coach Djoko Hadjilevski should give Australia the upper hand in their World Cup soccer warm-up match next week. Macedonia will be without five key foreign-based players, including forme Inter-Milan striker Darko Pancev. Page 47.
THE AGE

Australian distance swimmer Daniel Kowalski, due to defend his 1995 world shortcourse titles in the 400 metres freestyle and 1500 metres freestyle, may need to withdraw from the world shortcourse championships in Sweden next month because of an inflamed soulder. Page 14.

Australian Football League Brownlow medallist Michael Voss could play his first game since last year's semi-finals in Brisbane's Ansett Cup quarter-final against St Kilda at Waverly Park next Sunday night. Voss was a late withdrawal from last tear's preliinary final against North Melbourne because of a sprained ankle. Page 14.

Australian tennis sensation Mark Phillippoussis slammed the fastest serve of his career in his first-round victory at an ATP event in Arizona yesterday. In his defeat of wildcard entrant Tommy Haas of Germany, 2-6, 6-3, 6-4, Philippoussis smashed a serve of 222.4 kilometres per hour. Page 14.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian horse trainer Lee Freedman will recommend star filly Merlene be retired after she pulled up distressed in a trial at Flemington yesterday. Last year's Golden Slipper winner was operated on for breathing problems shortly after winning the AJC Sies' Produce Stakes at Randwick in early April last year, and has not raced since. Page 86.

Coca-Cola has become the new sponsor for Tennis Victoria's junior development program. Under the four-year deal, tens of thousands of dollars will go into category one and two development squads run by tennis associations and clubs throughout the State. Pge 77.

Australian Madison cycling champions Brett Aitken and Stephen Pate may not represent Australia at the world championships in Perth - even if they blitz the field at Bendigo on Sunday. The pair are favourites to win the 100 kilometre Bendigo Madison, yet erly indication do not mark them as certain selections for the Australian team. Page 79.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

North Queensland rugby league player Tyran Smith has escaped penalty on a high tackle charge but will serve an automatic one-match suspension if he goes into the sin-bin this season. Super League's opening premiership round resulted in commissioner Jim Hal sending warning notices to four players following kicking and high-tackle incidents. Page 70.

Juggler's managing owner Peter Horowitz has delayed until today a decision about taking on Octagonal in Monday's A$1.25 million Australian Cup at Flemington. Trainer Gai Waterhouse will meet with Horowitz today and should have a decision by the end of their talks. Page 66.

Penrith rugby league club's point scoring centre Ryan Girdler will play against Canberra at Bruce Stadium on Sunday with a fractured left hand. Girdler suffered the injury while playing the Perth Reds last Sunday and there were fears he might be out of acion for as long as six weeks. Page 68.
